description.description: Mobile UX design is the practice of designing mobile app and website user experiences for small screens and thumb-driven input. It covers information architecture, interaction patterns, visual design, performance, and accessibility. Good mobile UX is short, clear, and respects the context users are actually in (distracted, often in public, one-handed).

questions.name: What makes a good mobile UX?
questions.title: What makes a good mobile UX?

description.description: A good mobile UX gets users to value quickly, respects thumb-zone ergonomics, uses mobile-appropriate input methods, handles errors clearly, performs well on slower devices and networks, and adapts to intermittent connectivity. The best mobile UX designs feel fast, predictable, and forgiving of mistakes.

questions.name: What's the difference between mobile UX and desktop UX?
questions.title: What's the difference between mobile UX and desktop UX?

description.description: Mobile UX accounts for smaller screens, thumb-driven input, distracted contexts, variable network conditions, and wider device variance. Desktop UX assumes more controlled environments, keyboard and mouse input, larger screens, and stable networks. Patterns that work well on desktop (hover states, complex navigation, dense information) often fail on mobile.

questions.name: Is mobile UX design different from mobile UI design?
questions.title: Is mobile UX design different from mobile UI design?

description.description: Yes. UX (user experience) is the whole journey: how the user feels, how they navigate, how errors are handled, how fast things feel. UI (user interface) is specifically the visual and interactive surfaces: buttons, colors, typography, layout. UI is part of UX. You can have good UI with bad UX (a beautiful app that's confusing to use) or good UX with unfashionable UI (a utilitarian app that works perfectly).
